parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, facility ban, custody rule or documented current police targeting of trans visitors appears. But the dossier documents: a criminal statute (Arts. 520/517) reachable by a trans visitor, up to 3 years' imprisonment, with a documented (though 2010-era) enforcement history against private gatherings; no anti-discrimination protection and no complaint route (criminalisation of same-sex conduct removes the reporting channel after assault, refusal or document dispute); a suppressed public climate ('only in whispers', hubs eradicated, tour defunct); and armed-group killings/beatings for 'sodomy' in control zones, dated (2016) and without denominators so magnitude is unresolved. Unknowns (present police practice, trans-specific data) are resolved from structural signals — criminalisation, no recognition, unregistrable NGOs, weak rule of law. Statutory exposure plus no recourse plus hostile society puts this in the high-risk band, below documented-universal-exclusion cases; the 2025 debunking of a 'hunting' claim and absence of later raids keep it from lower tiers.
